sources.retreat: The audited retreat path at 0x624633 calls sub_5F5A4B. At 0x5F5A74..0x5F5AA8 that helper rejects Fort/Ruin groups and defending stacks with nonempty insideId (+0x94); an attacking stack is not rejected merely for having insideId.
sources.fear: CBatAttackFear vtable 0x6F3F3C. sub_65D15B calls the same sub_5F5A4B at 0x65D1D4 with the target group's attacking/defending role. onHit 0x65D06F checks that result: at 0x65D114 it sets status 0x1D (Retreating), or at 0x65D126 it sets status 2 (Paralyze) and records the current round via sub_623C09.

implementation: BattleState.battle_fort_defender snapshots none, blue or red at entry. It is independent of fortification armour and is cleared on battle completion/reset.
City/capital garrisons and visiting enemy armies are identified by their current settlement position; the mobile bot's home capital is included.
Pending attacks on the player's owned city/capital make BLUE the defender and RED the attacker. Attacking from a settlement never marks the attacker as its defender.
The same _can_retreat predicate guards action_mask, public step and tactical resolution, including queued escapes and instant-retreat equipment.
Primary Fear, secondary Fear and item Fear share _fear_protected and use the finite paralyzed flag for settlement defenders. Existing immunity and ward checks remain in force.

The environment's forced player retreat at its round limit is disabled for settlement defenders, with no forced-retreat event or penalty; the episode decision budget still applies. This is integration with the existing JAX limit, not a new claim about an original-game round cap.
scope: This change adds the requested city/capital retreat restriction. Existing fear handling for ruins and explicit scenario team overrides is retained; it is not used as a general prohibition on voluntary retreat.
